AB  - Introduction Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare and complex disorder with unknown incidence and prevalence. It is characterized by a classic triad of limb overgrowth with both capillary and venous malformation. Clinical manifestations include port-wine stain with underlying soft tissue and/or bony hypertrophy in the involved limb. Limb hypertrophy is usually noted at birth. While the overall course of the disease varies, it is often progressive with the affected limb growing out of proportion. MRI is the imaging study of choice for examination of the associated vascular abnormalities present in KTS. Complications include pain, soft-tissue infection, lymphedema, bleeding, and thromboembolism. Management of KTS requires a multidisciplinary approach including a range of specialists. Unfortunately, treatment is primarily supportive. Pain remains a significant source of morbidity in patients with KTS secondary to both the underlying disease process itself and the associated surgeries for the disease. Materials and methods (NA for case report) NA Results/Case report Our patient was an opioid naive male in his late twenties encountered perioperatively on the Anesthesia Acute Pain service. His medical history was significant for only for Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome with an affected right lower extremity and prehypertension. He initially presented to the emergency department at our institution with acute exacerbation of a chronic lower extremity ulcer which he had previously undergone surgical debridement for. Upon presentation he complained of hyperalgesia and burning dysesthesias in the affected limb and was admitted for further workup. Prior to surgery his pain was easily controlled by his primary team on low dose opioids. MRI of the right lower extremity revealed chronic soft tissue ulceration complicated by extensive subcutaneous and intramuscular venous varicosities. Vascular surgery was consulted and the patient underwent surgical debridement on hospital day 4 with an estimated total of 25cm<sup>2</sup> of tissue excised. The Anesthesia Acute Pain service was consulted on POD 1 for severe pain which was uncontrolled on high dose opioid medications. Upon our initial encounter the patient was in obvious extreme discomfort despite hydromorphone PCA. In addition to pain at the surgical site he complained of extreme burning pain and shooting pain with radiation down his right lower extremity. A multimodal pain management approach was initiating using both long and short acting oral opioids, gabapentin, toradol, and acetaminophen. The patient was discharged home on POD 5 with plans to follow up with the Anesthesia Pain service . Discussion Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare disorder which is characterized by limb overgrowth with associated vascular abnormalities most commonly seen in the lower extremities. The diagnosis is a clinical one with the extent of the disease best further assessed by MRI. The disease process is often progressive requiring a multimodal treatment approach. Morbidity is high in KTS and chronic pain remains a major source of this morbidity. Pain management in KTS is difficult but should focus on providing temporary relief while the underlying cause of the pain is targeted by surgical or other means. Management of the complex neuropathic pain present is difficult but has the potential to significantly decrease the overall morbidity of KTS.

AB  - Background Vascular Anomalies are common in children. By ISSVA classification they are divided into two main groups as Vascular Malformations and Vascular Tumours. Malformations persist throughout life while tumours regress with time in most cases. Objectives: To discuss various types of Vascular Anomalies. I will take the audience through the simplified classification set up by ISSVA followed by our experience at GOSH with respect to treatments of children'sVA with lasers. A brief reviewon our 23 years of experience will be presented. Study design/Material and method: This is incorporated in some of the work we have already done with laser technology, including using pulsed dye lasers, the multiplex and now combining both to achieve a better outcome for stubborn/recalcitrant port wine stains, complex vascular lesions and many other conditions we treat. Conclusion: Lasers have great benefit in their use for children with Vascular Anomalies. Without this technology and its applications there will be a huge disadvantage for many children who suffer unnecessary emotional and psychological ill health and in some cases medical ill health. I will attempt to present the application of lasers for VA and the significant progress that has been made in this field.

AB  - Background Port wine stains (PWS) congenital capillary malformations with significant burden on the patient's quality of life. Mainstay treatment includes single pass PDL with outcomes up to 75%. Aim of the study was to determine whether 'Triple therapy' combining Cynergy Multiplex (PDL/Nd:Yag) with a further pass of PDL represents an effective treatment for recalcitrant [rfPWS], and to objectively assess outcome with SIAscope data. Study Design/Materials, and Methods Children who have received Triple therapy for rfPWS, and for whom SIAscopy readings had been taken, were retrospectively identified (n = 9). They were treated 'first pass' with CYNERGYMultiplex (595 nm PDL + 1064 nm Nd:YAG) laser, and then re-treated with a 'second pass' of the PDL Perfecta Laser. Probes varied from 8 to 12 mm (median 10 mm), pulse durations were standardised to group three (PDL 6 ms, Nd:Yag 15 ms). Multiplex PDL treatment had a median fluency of 10 (Range: 9-11), Multiplex Nd:YAG had a median fluency of 60 (Range: 50-65). PDL perfecta had a median fluency of 7 (Range: 6-11. Cooling of lasered areas was achieved by iced water, cryo4 air flow system, and cooled ultrasound gel during multiplex treatment and by Dynamic Cooling Device and iced water during PDL. SIAscope readings were taken pre-treatment and at follow up. Results Study is on-going with follow-up continuing although early data suggests therapy decreases the absolute number of blood chromophores by 9.2% (SIAscope data). No adverse events were reported. Conclusions Triple pass therapy is an effective treatment for rfPWS. SIAscopy objectively judge outcomes to guide treatment during therapy.

AB  - Introduction: Acquired localized lipoatrophies (LL) are an infrequent type of lipoatrophy, especially in children, with only 13 cases found in the literature. They can be primary such as lipoatrophia semicircularis, centrifugalis abdominalis infantilis and involutiva; or secondary to an underlying primary condition (lupus profundus, morphea) or iatrogenic event such as injections. Objective: To review the clinical and epidemiological characteristics, clinical course, associated factors and treatment of pediatric patients with acquired LL seen at our institution during a 20-year period. Methodology: We retrospectively searched records of patients with the diagnosis of lipoatrophy seen at our institution from 1995 to 2015, and reviewed those with an acquired LL. Results: We identified 12 patients with the diagnosis, 7 were girls, with a median age at appearance of lesions of 2 years and 3 months. Nine patients had one atrophic plaque, but 3 had bilateral symmetric plaques on buttocks. Most frequent location was buttocks (7), abdomen with extension to groin and thigh or buttocks (3), leg or thigh (1 patient each). The time from lesion appearance to diagnosis was 6 months, and most cases (8) had a history of intramuscular injections on the site where the lipoatrophy developed. Only one patient had other clinical conditions or findings: one port-wine stain on the face. Three patients had biopsies done which showed granulomatous reaction to foreign body and atrophic fat lobules. We categorized our patients acquired LL according to the clinical characteristics and course as iatrogenic (8 patients), lipoatrophia centrifugalis abdominalis infantilis (2) and involutive (2). We treated 5 patients, 4 with hidroxychloroquine and 1 with tacrolimus. Follow up ranged from 6 months to 8 years; 5 patients had complete remission and in 7 the lesions remained stable. Conclusions: Our series reports the largest number of pediatric patients with acquired LL as well as the youngest ones. We found that the most frequent cause of acquired LL in our population was secondary to intramuscular injections, followed by primary acquired LL; the most frequent location being buttocks. None of our patients had any relevant clinical condition, and the clinical course was benign, regardless of treatment.

AB  - Background: Majority of neonatal cutaneous conditions are benign and self-limited. However some serious skin infection as well as specific birthmarks can be found. These conditions are distinctive and require proper management approach. Objective: The aim of this study is to identify various cutaneous findings which occur during the first 5 days of life. The data will therefore be applied in the future educational sources for both dermatologists and pediatricians. Method: A prospective study of the newborns at a tertiary care center in the northeast of Thailand was performed from September 2015 - 2016. Total amount of 1, 000 newborns were examined. IRB was approved (HE581270). Results: This study distributed neonatal cutaneous conditions into 4 categories including i) transient neonatal skin conditions, ii) pigmentary birthmarks, iii) vascular birthmarks and iv) other miscellaneous skin conditions. Among transient neonatal skin conditions, sebaceous gland hyperplasia was the most common findings found during the study period (60.9%), followed by erythema toxicum neonatorum (22.2%) and milia (20.1%). Other transient neonatal skin conditions weremiliaria, neonatal acne, vernix caseosa and cutis marmorata. Among the pigmentary birthmarks, Mongolian spots were the most common findings with the percentage of 66.7%. The most frequent size of Mongolian spots was less than 5 cm in diameter (45.7%) with the most frequent location on buttock area. Salmon patches were the most frequent vascular birthmarks found in this study (26%). The most frequent location of salmon patches was on upper eyelids. The other vascular birthmarks found were infantile hemangiomas (1.1%) and port wine stain (0.7%). There was also the occurrence of bullous impetigo in 8 cases (0.8%). Three from eight cases were found with the presence of maternal fever; however, there were not statistical significant. Conclusions: Mongolian spot and sebaceous gland hyperplasia were the two most common cutaneous conditions found in Thai population. Even though majority of the neonatal cutaneous conditions were benign and self-limited; however, the right diagnosis among various cutaneous conditions is important which can be leaded to prompt specific action if necessary. Importantly, pediatric dermatologists should be familiar with the various birthmarks and become more comfortable discussing disease prevention and cosmetic strategies.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background: Asymptomatic infants with high-risk distribution port-wine stain (PWS) are commonly screened for Sturge-Weber Syndrome (SWS) using brainmagnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The incidence of false negative MRI scans is unknown, but false reassurance may delay the recognition and treatment of seizures and impact neuro developmental outcomes. Objective: We examine the impact of early MRI screening of high risk PWS on seizure detection. Methods and Results: A retrospective chart review was conducted of children with facial PWS presenting to the outpatient laser-clinic of the Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, a tertiary paediatric hospital between December 2015 and November 2016. Of 126 children with facial PWS, 9 (7.14%) had SWS, the association of a facial PWS with a capillary-venous malformation of the brain/leptomeninges and/or of the eye. 7/9 (77.78%) patients with SWS had high-risk (hemi-facial and median) PWS phenotypes according to recent classifications. Of the 4 patients with SWS with screening MRI's, false negatives occurred in 3 (75%). All false negative MRIs occurred before the age of 9 weeks. 2/3 (66.67%) of those with false negative scans received no specialised counselling about seizure recognition prior to the onset of seizures. Children with SWS who received early neurological assessment and seizure education had their first seizure detected at younger ages, whereas early MRI did not reduce the age of first seizure detection in our cohort. Screening electroence phalography (EEG) was performed in 2/9 patients. Both were abnormal, with sub-clinical seizures detected in one child 2 months before becoming clinically evident. Conclusion: Early MRI may give false negative results in infants and appears to have limited value in the management of high risk PWS. Conversely, there is a role for early neurological referral, symptom education and potentially of EEGs in the prevention of complications related to SWS.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Introduction Sturge-Weber Syndrome (SWS) is a rare neuro-cutaneous syndrome characterised by facial port-wine naevus and leptomeningeal angiomatosis that can be associated with neurological and ophthalmological complications. In its rare variant-SWS type 3, the clinical hallmark of facial naevus is absent which poses a diagnostic challenge. Here we present an interesting case of SWS type 3 who was admitted with prolonged severe unilateral headache mimicking migraine status. Case presentation A 9 year old alert boy presented with a 24 hour history of vomiting and severe left temporal headache. His initial neurological examination including fundal examination was normal. Urgent CT head with contrast showed calcification in left occipital cortical and sub-cortical lobe. He had a previous admission with severe headache and prolonged seizure 3 years ago, which was managed as presumed encephalitis. On day 3 of admission, he developed a dense right sided homonymous hemianopia. Urgent MRI brain with contrast showed pial angiomatosis in the occipital and parietal lobes along with atrophy of underlying cortex consistent with the diagnosis of SWS. His headaches slowly got better but after 2 days he developed complex partial seizure and was started on regular anti-epileptic medication. On follow up after 6 weeks, he has remained seizure free with occasional mild headaches. His visual field defect has improved slightly and he is under regular neurology and ophthalmology follow-up. Discussion SWS is a non-familial neurological disorder and has an incidence of 1:50 000 live births. SWS type 3 has only 24 cases reported in literature. SWS Type 3 is associated with a vascular malformation in the brain with no facial naevus and no glaucoma. It can have varied presentations such as seizures and as in our case headaches and visual field defects. It can only be identified through neuro-imaging with contrast,therefore it can be difficult to diagnose and does require high degree of suspicion. Learning Points This case highlights that it is important to have high index of suspicion and low threshold for neuroimaging (with contrast) in the cases presenting with prolonged severe headaches. SWS type 3 does exist and can mimic as migraine status as the presenting feature!

AB  - Laser treatment of the periocular skin is challenging primarily due to the risk of damage to the eye. Safety concerns of treating this site have to be appropriately addressed. We present our experience of laser treatment of periocular skin lesions in a random sample of 7 patients (3 males, 4 females) aged between 19 and 58 years. We used the Q-switched-Alexandrite laser (Qs-Al) to treat minocycline induced pigmentation and eyeliner tattoo migration; Qs Nd:YAG 1064 nm laser for traumatic tattoo; carbon dioxide (CO2) laser to ablate milia and trichoepitheliomata and pulsed dye laser (PDL) for port wine stain and post radiotherapy telangiectases. Intraocular protective eyeshields were placed pre-treatment. Successful response to treatment was observed in all patients. Laser epilation of eyebrows proves a challenge due to the anatomical structure, and has the highest risk of intraocular complications.Whilst challenging, most laser treatments can be safely undertaken for periocular skin lesions. Adequate protection of the globe with intraocular eye-shields is mandatory to protect the cornea and retina when using light in visible and near infrared regions.

AB  - Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is the commonest overgrowth cancer predisposition disorder and represents a model for human imprinting dysregulation and tumorigenesis. BWS features can variably combine and present a widely variable range of severity in the phenotypic expression. This wide spectrum is paralleled at molecular level by complex (epi)genetic defects on chromosome 11p15.5 leading to disrupted expression of imprinted genes controlling growth and cellular proliferation. In this review, we outline the spectrum of clinical manifestations of BWS analyzing their (epi)genotype-phenotype correlations. The differences observed in the phenotypic profiles of BWS molecular subtypes allow a composite view of this syndrome with implications on clinical care, diagnosis, follow-up, and management, and provide directions for future disease monitoring. AB  - Laser treatment of vascular lesions is affected by parameters including the diameter and depth of the vessels and flow within the vessels. Topical anaesthetics are in common use prior to laser treatment but may have effects on vessel parameters and, subsequently, the efficacy of laser treatment. Eleven patients with capillary vascular malformations were investigated for vessel diameter before and after elective application of a topical anaesthetic, Eutectic Mixture of Local Anaesthetics (EMLA) (AstraZeneca) or Ametop (S&N Health), prior to pulsed dye laser treatment. EMLA contains 2.5 % lidocaine ad 2.5 % prilocaine, and Ametop gel contains 4 % tetracaine. Patients' capillary malformations were assessed using confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) (Vivascope 1500 Mavig GmbH, Munich). Six of the 11 patients recruited had EMLA topical anaesthetic, and five had Ametop. Four hundred twenty-one diameters were measured. The mean vessel diameter was 50.87 mum. Previous laser treatments undergone by each patient were noted to exclude this as a confounding variable, and no significant difference was found between topical anaesthetic groups. Statistical calculations were made using GenStat and Minitab. There is no evidence that Ametop affects mean diameter (p value is 0.361). EMLA reduces the mean diameter of vessels (p = 0.002), with a 27 % reduction in post-EMLA diameter. This study demonstrates that the use of EMLA cream has a statistically significant reduction vessel diameter. As it is known that vessel diameter is important for the response of laser treatment, the use of EMLA may affect outcome. Copyright © 2016, Springer-Verlag London.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Purpose and background: We describe three paediatric cases with different intracranial fast-flow shunts presenting early in life, all with capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome and RASA1 verified mutations. Intracranial arteriovenous fast-flow shunts are rare vascular malformations typically presenting early in life and have been associated with cutaneous capillary malformations, characterized as capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome. Heterozygous RASA1 gene mutations have been found to be disease causing with high penetrance for the typical cutaneous findings, but only some individuals with the syndrome have intracranial lesions. Cases: One infant presented with a vein of Galen malformation responsible for hydrodynamic disorders, one neonate suffered from severe cardiac insufficiency related to a superior sagittal sinus dural malformation with high-flow fistulas, and one baby was treated at infant age of a choroidal arteriovenous fistula discovered antenatally. Results and conclusions: We report the follow-up of these three cases with RASA1 gene mutation and comment on the possible role of evaluation for vascular lesions and capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome in patients and their families, with intracranial fast-flow shunts. TY  - JOUR
AB  - Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is characterized by cancer predisposition, overgrowth and highly variable association of macroglossia, abdominal wall defects, nephrourological anomalies, nevus flammeus, ear malformations, hypoglycemia, hemihyperplasia, and organomegaly. BWS molecular defects, causing alteration of expression or activity of the genes regulated by two imprinting centres (IC) in the 11p15 chromosomal region, are also heterogeneous. In this paper we define (epi)genotype-phenotype correlations in molecularly confirmed BWS patients. The characteristics of 318 BWS patients with proven molecular defect were compared among the main four molecular subclasses: IC2 loss of methylation (IC2-LoM, n=190), IC1 gain of methylation (IC1-GoM, n=31), chromosome 11p15 paternal uniparental disomy (UPD, n=87), and cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1C gene (CDKN1C) variants (n=10). A characteristic growth pattern was found in each group; neonatal macrosomia was almost constant in IC1-GoM, postnatal overgrowth in IC2-LoM, and hemihyperplasia more common in UPD (P<0.001). Exomphalos was more common in IC2/CDKN1C patients (P<0.001). Renal defects were typical of UPD/IC1 patients, uretheral malformations of IC1-GoM cases (P<0.001). Ear anomalies and nevus flammeus were associated with IC2/CDKN1C genotype (P<0.001). Macroglossia was less common among UPD patients (P<0.001). Wilms' tumor was associated with IC1-GoM or UPD and never observed in IC2-LoM patients (P<0.001). Hepatoblastoma occurred only in UPD cases. Cancer risk was lower in IC2/CDKN1C, intermediate in UPD, and very high in IC1 cases (P=0.009). In conclusion, (epi)genotype-phenotype correlations define four different phenotypic BWS profiles with some degree of clinical overlap. These observations impact clinical care allowing to move toward (epi) genotype-based follow-up and cancer screening. Copyright © 2016 Macmillan Publishers Limited All rights reserved.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - PIK3CA-related overgrowth syndrome (PROS) was recently agreed upon as an umbrella term to encompass the variety of phenotypes associated with somatic mutations in the PIK3CA gene. Several mosaic overgrowth syndromes that were previously described as separate entities are now known to share this common cause, with continuation and overlap between diagnoses. We present a patient with a somatic mutation in PIK3CA, whose phenotype would previously have been most consistent with a diagnosis of megalencephaly-capillary malformation syndrome (MCAP). A 2-year-old boy presented at birth with a weight of 5.02 kg and an episode of neonatal hypoglycaemia. A widespread capillary malformation was noted, affecting his trunk and limbs. In addition he had a persistent naevus flammeus and an infantile haemangioma. Signs of overgrowth included hemihypertrophy of the left leg and a head circumference on the 99.6th centile. He had mild developmental delay. In view of the hypoglycaemia and overgrowth he was initially investigated for Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome, which was ruled out on the basis of normal 11p15 methylation studies. DNA from blood lymphocytes was analysed for a PIK3CA mutation; this was also negative. Clinical suspicion of MCAP persisted, and a skin biopsy was performed to test for a mutation in affected skin fibroblasts. This confirmed a mosaic heterozygous variant in PIK3CA, p.Glu453del. PIK3CA encodes the catalytic subunit of phosphatidylinositol-3-kinase, part of the mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) pathway, and this variant causes gain of function leading to excessive growth in affected tissue. Other conditions caused by mutations in genes in this pathway include Proteus syndrome and Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome. Knowledge of the PIK3CA/AKT/mTOR pathway has meant that clinical trials of mTOR inhibitors are now under way, in an attempt to control tissue overgrowth in these patients, although at present the overgrowth in our patient is not severe enough to require treatment. DNA analysis from affected tissue is a necessary technique in diagnosing somatic mosaic disorders, and this investigation should be considered in children if there is clinical likelihood of an overgrowth disorder.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Thorium X is an ionizing, topical radiation treatment previously used in the 1930s to treat vascular lesions, including port-wine stains (PWSs) and benign dermatoses. By the 1960s it was discontinued due to poor results and recognition of its carcinogenic potential. The occurrence of a basal cell carcinoma (BCC) within a PWS is rare but has been associated with prior radiation treatment. We describe our experience of three cases of BCCs occurring within PWSs following previous thorium X treatment. All were treated successfully with Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS). A 73-year-old man presented with an enlarging, bleeding lesion on his right cheek at the site of a PWS. Examination revealed a shiny, erythematous plaque (30 x 20 mm), confirmed on biopsy as an infiltrative BCC and treated with one-stage MMS. Our second patient was a 75-year-old woman presenting with two nonhealing lesions on her right infraorbital cheek, within a longstanding PWS. Examination showed multiple lesions representing BCCs (35 x 28 mm) affecting the right infraorbital cheek within the PWS. Biopsy confirmed multiple nodular and superficial BCC, which required two stages of MMS. This led to complete loss of the right lower eyelid. Our third patient was a 67-year-old woman presenting with lesions within an extensive PWS. Examination revealed firm nodules in the left nasolabial fold and ala. Histology confirmed multiple nodular BCCs and MMS was performed. In all three cases more tumours were encountered during MMS, and thus the defect was more extensive than initially anticipated. Two cases were reconstructed with a full-thickness skin graft and the other with a rotation flap. BCCs have been reported in PWS without the presence of thorium X; however, the application of a carcinogenic material increases the risk of malignant formation. It has been suggested that either the increased temperature induced by the increased dermal vasculature or an oncogenic factor produced by the ectatic vessels can make the overlying epidermis more susceptible to ionizing radiation (Lapidoth M, Ad-El D, David M et al. Basal cell carcinoma arising over facial port wine stain: a single centre experience. J Eur Acad Dermatol Venereol 2006; 20: 1066-9). Due to this significant association, dermatologists should carefully assess for BCCs in patients with thorium X-treated PWS. MMS is the treatment of choice in these cases, as there are often multiple indistinct BCCs within the PWS.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background: Several cellular functions relate to ion-channels activity. Physiologically relevant chains of events leading to angiogenesis, cell cycle and different forms of cell death, require transmembrane voltage control. We hypothesized that the unordered angiogenesis occurring in solid cancers and vascular malformations might associate, at least in part, to ion-transport alteration. Methods: The expression level of several ion-channels was analyzed in human solid tumor biopsies. Expression of 90 genes coding for ion-channels related proteins was investigated within the Oncomine database, in 25 independent patients-datasets referring to five histologically-different solid tumors (namely, bladder cancer, glioblastoma, melanoma, breast invasive-ductal cancer, lung carcinoma), in a total of 3673 patients (674 control-samples and 2999 cancer-samples). Furthermore, the ion-channel activity was directly assessed by measuring in vivo the electrical sympathetic skin responses (SSR) on the skin of 14 patients affected by the flat port-wine stains vascular malformation, i.e., a non-tumor vascular malformation clinical model. Results: Several ion-channels showed significantly increased expression in tumors (p < 0.0005); nine genes (namely, CACNA1D, FXYD3, FXYD5, HTR3A, KCNE3, KCNE4, KCNN4, CLIC1, TRPM3) showed such significant modification in at least half of datasets investigated for each cancer type. Moreover, in vivo analyses in flat port-wine stains patients showed a significantly reduced SSR in the affected skin as compared to the contralateral healthy skin (p < 0.05), in both latency and amplitude measurements. Conclusions: All together these data identify ion-channel genes showing significantly modified expression in different tumors and cancer-vessels, and indicate a relevant electrophysiological alteration in human vascular malformations. Such data suggest a possible role and a potential diagnostic application of the ion-electron transport in vascular disorders underlying tumor neo-angiogenesis and vascular malformations. AB  - Background Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is a congenital overgrowth disorder predisposing to tumorigenesis that results from abnormal expression or function of imprinted genes of chromosome 11p15.5. Methods Forty-seven patients in Taiwan with clinical suspicion of BWS were referred for diagnostic testing based on methylation profiling of H19-associated imprinting center (IC) 1 and KCNQ1OT1-associated IC2 using high-resolution melting analysis, multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification, or high-resolution quantitative methylation profiling. Results Twenty-eight patients received a clinical diagnosis of BWS (the presence of 3 major features or 2 major features and at least 1 minor feature), 18 had suspected BWS (the presence of at least 1 major feature), and 1 had isolated Wilms' tumor. Nineteen patients were identified with IC2 hypomethylation (including 1 with isolated Wilms' tumor), 1 with IC1 hypermethylation, 2 with paternal uniparental disomy, and 1 with CDKN1C mutation. Several clinical features were found to be statistically different (P < 0.05) between the 2 groups-clinical diagnosis of BWS (n = 28) or suspected BWS (n = 18)-including macroglossia, pre- or postnatal gigantism, abdominal wall defect, ear creases, facial nevus flammeus, BWS score, and the molecular diagnosis rate. Molecular lesion was detected in 81% of patients with the presence of three major features, compared with 33% and 28% of those with two or one major feature, respectively. The mean BWS score was 5.6 for 19 subjects with "IC2 hypomethylation", compared with 3.8 for 2 subjects with pUPD. The BWS score of one subject with CDKN1C mutation and one with IC1 hypermethylation was 6 and 7, respectively. Conclusions The BWS score was positively correlated with the molecular diagnosis rate (P < 0.01). The BWS database of epigenotype, genotype, and phenotype is expected to promote better genetic counseling and medical care of these patients. Copyright © 2016

AB  - Characterizing port wine stains (PWS) with its optical parameters [i.e. absorption coefficient (mu<inf>a</inf>) and reduced scattering coefficient (mu<inf>s</inf>')] and microvascular parameters [i.e. blood volume fraction (BVF), mean vessel diameter (MVD), and oxygen saturation (StO<inf>2</inf>)] is extremely important for elucidating the mechanisms for its light-based treatments, such as pulsed dye laser and photodynamic therapy. In this study, a customized diffuse reflectance spectroscopy (DRS) probe with an appropriate source-detector distance was used to measure the diffuse reflectance spectra of PWS lesions in clinical practice. The results demonstrate that optical parameters of different types of PWS lesions can be accurately extracted by fitting the DRS with diffusion equation. Since the sampling depth of the probe coincides with the depth distribution of abnormal vasculature in PWS, the obtained microvascular parameters of PWS lesions that changed from pink to purple are in agreement with the corresponding physiological conditions. This study suggests that DRS can be utilized to quantitatively determine the optical and microvascular parameters of PWS lesions, which have the potential for planning the protocol and predicting the efficiency for light-based PWS treatments. AB  - Purpose: To evaluate choroidal thickness and its effect on the outer retinal layers in patients with Sturge Weber syndrome (SWS). Materials and methods: Twenty eyes of 10 patients with SWS and 20 eyes of 10 healthy controls were evaluated at the ophthalmology unit of the Umberto I Policlinic, Rome from December 2015 to May 2015. Manual segmentation measurements of choroidal and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE)-photorec eptor layer (PHL) thickness were performed at the subfovea and at 500 micro m intervals over 3 mm-long horizontal and vertical segments using enhanced depth spectral domain optical coherence tomography. Results: Mean choroidal thickness of the affected (561.6 micro m +/- 208.8) and fellow eyes (322.0 micro m +/- 56.6) of patients with SWS was significantly higher with respect to controls (266.5 micro m +/- 48.5 micro m), p = 0.001 and p = 0.017, respectively. Mean RPE-PHL thickness was significantly lower in both the affected and fellow eyes of patients with respect to controls (p = 0.039 and p = 0.025, respectively). Conclusions: The choroid is thickened in patients with SWS, but the RPE-PHL is thinner. Choroidal thickening may lead to functional impairment causing disruption in the fine equilibrium between the choroid and retina and consequent outer retinal layer thinning. AB  - Background Port wine stains (PWSs) are commonly treated by the pulsed dye laser. However, treatment of hypertrophic or resistant PWSs is a major therapeutic challenge. The long-pulsed Alexandrite laser could be a safe and effective treatment for resistant PWSs, due to an increase depth of penetration of 50-75% over PDL. Objective The aim of this study was to assess the efficacy and safety of a long-pulsed Alexandrite laser in patients with hypertrophic, dark and/or resistant PWSs. Pink pale resistant PWS were excluded from the study. Methods Twenty-one patients (age 20-75 years), phototypes I-IV on the Fitzpatrick scale, with PDL dark resistant PWSs were treated with long-pulsed Alexandrite laser. We excluded high phototypes and PDL pink resistant PWSs. All patients were treated with 3 laser sessions at settings of 3-ms pulse duration, 10-mm spot, 35-55 J/cm<sup>2</sup>, with cooling (Dynamic Cooling Device 50 ms with delay 30 ms). Laser sessions were repeated approximately every 2 months. Three dermatologists evaluated treatment effectiveness by means of photographs of the patients before and after laser treatment (scale from 0 to 4). Adverse events were registered. Patient satisfaction was also assessed (scale from 0 to 10). Results Mean global improvement was rated as 2.28. Long-lasting side effects included minimal scarring after blistering in 1 patient. Mean patient satisfaction was 8.5. Conclusions Our study concludes that long-pulsed Alexandrite laser was effective for treatment of resistant PWSs, although the therapeutical window is narrow with this treatment. AB  - Background Among the different approaches for improving the effectiveness in the treatment of Capillary Malformations type Port Wine Stain (CM type PWS) are the intense pulsed light sources. There are few clinical studies prove useful in the treatment of CM. Furthermore, no studies have been published yet demonstrating the histological effects of IPL in CM. Objectives To assess the histological effects of pulsed light in capillary malformations type port wine stain. We wanted to compare epidermal, dermal and vessel wall damage after treatment with different combinations of IPL parameters. Material and methods Fifty-five post-treatment biopsies were performed in 15 consenting patients with CM and stained with nitroblue-tetrazolium chloride (NBTC). Patients had not been treated previously. Results Fifteen patients with CM, with a median age of 39 years-old were enrolled in this study. In this series, the patients with the most severe epidermal damage were those with a darker phototype. Pink CM were especially resistant to treatment, even using high fluences, short pulse durations and stacking pulses. Longer intra- and interpulse delays were effective in purple CM, achieving adequate vessel destruction. Conclusions IPL devices provide a vast amount of treatment possibilities and further studies are necessary to optimize therapeutic approaches to CM. In this study we have observed the histological effects of different pulses on the MC type PWS. Copyright © 2015 AEDV.

AB  - Phacomatosis pigmentovascularis is a rare group of syndromes characterized by the co-existence of a vascular nevus and a pigmentary nevus with or without extracutaneous systemic involvement. The existing classifications of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis are based on phenotypic characteristics. We report four new cases of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis, three with phacomatosis cesioflammea demonstrating phenotypic variability, and one with phacomatosis cesiomarmorata. Extracutaneous manifestations were observed in three patients (75%) that included central nervous system involvement in three, bilateral congenital glaucoma in two, and cardiovascular system involvement in one. The molecular basis of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis is yet to be elucidated. Whether the various subtypes of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis are separate molecular entities or phenotypic variants of the same disease needs to be settled. AB  - Objective: The objective of this study was to monitor blood perfusion dynamics of port wine stains (PWS) during vascular targeted photodynamic therapy (V-PDT) with laser Doppler imaging (LDI). Methods: The PWS lesions of 30 facial PWS patients received V-PDT, while the normal skins on the forearm of 5 healthy subjects were treated as light-only controls for comparison. Furthermore, two different PWS lesions in the same individual from each of 3 PWS patients successively received laser irradiation only and V-PDT, respectively. LDI was used to monitor intraoperative blood perfusion dynamics. Results: During V-PDT, the blood perfusion (278 +/- 96 PU) in PWS lesions for 31 of 33 PWS patients significantly increased after the initiation of V-PDT treatment, then reached a peak (638 +/- 105 PU) within 10 min, followed by a slow decrease to a relatively lower level (515 +/- 100 PU). Furthermore, the time for reaching peak and the subsequent magnitude of decrease in blood perfusion varied with different patients. For light-only controls, an initial perfusion peak at 3 min followed by a nadir and a secondary increase were found not only in normal skin, but also in PWS lesions. Conclusion: The preliminary results showed that the LDI permits non-invasive monitoring blood perfusion changes of PWS lesions during V-PDT. There was a clear trend in blood perfusion responses during V-PDT and laser irradiation. The blood perfusion changes during treatment were due to V-PDT effects as well as local temperature increase induced by laser irradiation. Copyright © 2016 Elsevier B.V.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background and Objective A port wine stain (PWS) is a type of capillary vascular malformation composed of malformed, dilated blood vessels within the papillary and reticular dermis. Currently, pulsed dye laser (PDL) is considered the therapeutic gold standard, although greater than 90% of lesions may be refractory to treatment. Studies have shown that a delay in treatment results in a higher proportion of patients who develop hypertrophy and nodularity within lesions that become more resistant to therapy. Therapeutic resistance is multifactorial, but is believed to be largely due to revascularization after laser treatment. Oral sirolimus and topical imiquimod have shown promise as adjunctive therapies to minimize post-laser revascularization, but both have significant side effects. We wish to demonstrate the utility of adjunct topical sirolimus to reduce revascularization after PDL treatment. Study Design/Patients and Methods This is a single patient case report of a 56-year-old male patient with an extensive PWS. After seeing initial improvement with PDL alone, he began to experience thickening and nodularity of his PWS necessitating surgical debulking. Since this procedure, topical sirolimus 0.5% ointment has been added to his treatment regimen as an adjunct to PDL. The patient is being treated with PDL (Vbeam Perfecta, Candela/Syneron, Wayland, MA) every 4-6 weeks at varied settings with the following laser parameters: fluence 9-11 J/cm<sup>2</sup>, pulse duration 0.45-1.5 ms, focal spot size 7 mm, cooling 30/20. Sirolimus 0.5% ointment is applied to the area twice daily. Results The patient showed significant improvement in color and texture of his PWS. Compared to the initial therapy of PDL alone, topical sirolimus ointment in conjunction with PDL demonstrated greater improvement and maintenance of therapeutic results with fewer overall laser treatments. Conclusion Topical sirolimus 0.5% ointment is a safe and effective adjunct to PDL in the treatment of PWS. Copyright © 2015 Wiley Periodicals, Inc.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background Pulsed dye lasers have revolutionized treatment of port-wine stains (PWS). The authors' previous study with a 585-nm/0.45-millisecond pulsed dye laser (PDL) showed 25% to 75% improvement in 60% of facial PWS. METHODS The authors analyzed data on facial PWS treated with a 595-nm tunable PDL in Indian patients. Response was assessed subjectively on a scale of 21 to 5 (Investigator Global Assessment) by comparing pretreatment and posttreatment photographs. Patients' perception of change in PWS was also noted on a visual analog scale from 0 to 10 (Patient Global Assessment). Side effects were recorded. RESULTS A total of 74 flat and 24 hypertrophic PWS in skin Types IV and V with a median lesion size of 56 cm<sup>2</sup> and 10<sup>2</sup> cm<sup>2</sup>, respectively, and color ranging from pink to purple were treated. They underwent a mean of 7.3 and 8.5 sessions (range: 4-10 session), respectively. A mean lightening of 54% in flat and 40% in hypertrophic PWS was observed. After 10 treatments, 46.6% of flat PWS cases showed >75% lightening and an equal number had 25% to 75% improvement. A >75% improvement was observed in 12.5% of hypertrophic PWS with 75% of cases showing between 25% to 75% improvement. No significant side effects were noted. CONCLUSION The 595-nm tunable PDL produced moderate response with no significant side effects. Copyright © 2016 by the American Society for Dermatologic Surgery, Inc.

AB  - PURPOSE: Our study aim was to clarify the characteristics of hemangiomas with pseudo washout sign (PWS) by comparing their features with those of hemangiomas without PWS on gadolinium-ethoxybenzyl-diethylenetriaminepentaacetic acid (Gd-EOB-DTPA)-enhanced magnetic resonance (MR) imaging. METHODS: We evaluated the features of hemangiomas on Gd-EOB-DTPA-enhanced MR imaging of 70 hepatic hemangiomas in 31 patients, investigating the presence of peripheral or central nodular enhancement, diffuse enhancement, and arterioportal shunt during the arterial phase, fill-in enhancement during the portal venous phase, and PWS, which is low signal intensity during the late phase. We visually assessed the intensity of contrast enhancement of the lesion during the arterial, portal venous, late, and hepatobiliary phases using a 4-grade scale and used the Fisher exact and Mann-Whitney U tests to compare hemangiomas with and without PWS. RESULTS: We observed PWS in 33 (47%) of 70 hemangiomas, which were significantly smaller than the hemangiomas without PWS (17.4 mm +/- 20.3 versus 30.1 mm +/- 28.5; P = 0.005); more frequent diffuse enhancement in hemangiomas with PWS than those without (21.2% versus 2.7%; P = 0.026); and no significant differences in nodular enhancement (P = 0.231), arterioportal shunt (P = 0.403), or fill-in enhancement (P = 0.357) between hemangiomas with and without PWS. Visually determined grades of tumor contrast enhancement were significantly lower in hemangiomas with PWS during the portal venous (P = 0.007) and late (P < 0.001) phases. CONCLUSIONS: Small hemangiomas tend to decrease in signal intensity during the portal venous phase and show PWS during the late phase.

AB  - Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome is a rarely encountered congenital disease characterized by a triad of enlarged arteries and veins, limb hypertrophy and capillary malformations. We are presenting an interesting case of a 23-year male who had been previously diagnosed to have Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome. The patient presented with large pulmonary embolism after having undergone laser surgery for varicose veins. The diagnostic chest computed tomography (CT) performed also revealed the co-existence of severe destructive pulmonary parenchymal disease involving large areas of the pulmonary parenchyma and formation of large emphysematous bullae having an asymmetric involvement of the left lung field. The patient was managed with thrombolysis with a bolus fibrinolytic agent and subsequently underwent an inferior vena cava (IVC) filter implantation to prevent further episodes of embolism in the presence of a compromised lung. The association of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome with recurrent pulmonary embolism and unexplained pulmonary parenchymal disease leading to almost complete destruction of large areas of lung fields is interesting and has never been previously described.

AB  - A case of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis combined with congenital preauricular fistula is reported. A 4-month old girl presented with massive nevus flammeus on the face, trunk, upper extremities, and Mongolian spots on the trunk and legs. The lesions on the right side were much worse. A preauricular fistula with 2 mm in diameter was found on the both ears. laboratory and auxiliary examinations showed normal for routine blood and urine tests, liver and kidney function, echocardiography and cerebral CT scanning. The Diagnosis of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis combined with congenital preauricular fistula was made. Patient was given a single treatment with dye pulse laser, and has been closely followed up.

AB  - We proposed and developed a photoacoustic (PA) dermoscope equipped with an integrated PA probe to achieve quantification and high-resolution, high-contrast deep imaging of human skin. The PA probe, with light-sound confocal excitation and reception, is specially designed, and integrated with an objective lens, an ultrasound transducer, and an inverted-triangle coupling cup to facilitate convenient implementation in a clinical setting. The PA dermoscope was utilized for noninvasive and high-resolution imaging of epidermal and dermal structure in volunteers. The imaging results demonstrated that the characteristic parameters of skin disease, including pigment distribution and thickness, vascular diameter, and depth, can be obtained by the PA dermoscope, confirming that PA dermoscopy can serve as a potential tool for the diagnosis and curative effect evaluation of human skin disease. TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background and Objectives: Photodynamic therapy (PDT) has shown potentially beneficial results in treating port-wine stain, but its benefit-risk profile remains undefined. This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of PDT conducted with hemoporfin and a 532 nm continuous wave laser to treat port-wine stain clinically. Patients and Methods: This randomized clinical trial was conducted in eight hospitals in China. Participants were adolescent and adult patients (age range: 14-65 years old) with port-wine stain. During stage 1 (day 1 to week 8) all patients were randomized at a 3:1 ratio to treatment (532 nm laser irradiation (96-120 J/cm<sup>2</sup>) with hemoporfin (5mg/kg; PDT-hemoporfin, n = 330)) or placebo groups (irradiation with placebo (PDT-placebo, n = 110)); during stage 2 (week 8 to 16) patients in both groups were offered treatment. Clinician-evaluators, who were blind to the study, classified each case on the following four-level scale according to assessment of before and after standardized pictures of the lesion area: no improvement: <20%; some improvement: 20-59%; great improvement: 60-89%; or nearly completely resolved: >=90%. The primary efficacy endpoint was proportion of patients achieving at least some improvement at week 8. The secondary efficacy endpoints were proportion of patients achieving nearly completely resolved or at least great improvement at week 8, proportion of patients achieving early completely resolved, at least great improvement, or at least some improvement at week 16, and the corresponding satisfaction of the investigators and the patients (designated as 'excellent', 'good', 'moderate', or'ineffective') at weeks 8 and 16. Results: Compared to the PDT-placebo group, the PDT-hemoporfin group showed a significantly higher proportion of patients that achieved at least some improvement (89.7% [n = 295; 95% CI, 85.9%-92.5%] vs. 24.5% [n = 27; 95% CI, 17.4%-33.3%]) at week 8 (P > 0.0001) and higher improvements for all secondary efficacy endpoints. Treatment reactions occurred in 99.5% (n = 731; 95% CI, 98.7%-99.8%) of the PDT-hemoporfin treatments (n = 735). Hyperpigmentation occurred in 22.9 per 100 patient-treatments (n = 168; 95% CI, 20.0-26.0) in the PDT-hemoporfin treated patients. Conclusions: Hemoporfin-mediated PDT is an effective and safe treatment option for adolescent and adult patients with port-wine stain. Trial Registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry ChiCTR-TRC-08000213. Copyright © 2016 Zhao et al. AB  - BACKGROUND: Flashlamp-pumped pulsed (FLPP) dye laser still represents the standard treatment for the majority of port wine stains (PWSs), but the results on thick PWSs remain unpredictable, and many of these lesions fail to completely respond. Our aim was to report on the results obtained on unresponsive PWSs to standard laser treatments, by using a double phase laser treatment strategy using two laser passes in the same session. METHODS: Eleven adult patients with facial PWS resistant to dye laser were enrolled. Laser sessions were scheduled every 8 weeks, and each of them consisting of two laser passes. In phase one, two different laser wavelengths (595 nm and 1064 nm) were delivered consecutively to each affected area. In the second phase, the PWS was treated using a pulse stacking technique with the 1064 nm Nd:YAG. RESULTS: One patient was lost to follow-up. Among the remaining ten, 5 (50%) patients showed an excellent improvement (>75%), 3 (30%) patients showed a good improvement (51-75%), and 2 (20%) patients had no or minimal improvement (0-25%). CONCLUSION: Our results suggest that the combination of different wavelengths in the same session can be helpful for PWSs resistant to standard laser treatments. However, in most patients two treatment phases were necessary. Copyright © 2014 EDIZIONI MINERVA MEDICA.

AB  - In the past few years, great advances concerning the study of vascular anomalies have been made in the hopes of unifying criteria in terms of classification and terminology, as well as on the therapeutic approach. Two large groups constitute vascular anomalies: vascular tumors and vascular malformations. Infantile hemangiomas represent the most important group within vascular tumors and are the most frequent benign childhood tumor. Even though, the majority have an indolent behaviour and spontaneous resolution, it is important to keep in mind that some hemangiomas, fundamentally due to their location, may cause vital risk to the patient as well as medical and aesthetic complications. On the other hand, within the vascular malformation group, the Port wine stain is the most frequent. In contrast to hemangioma behaviour, vascular malformations do not involute and persist a lifetime. Therefore, it is crucial for the paediatrician to differentiate between these two groups, in order to establish a correct diagnosis and offer an ideal treatment for the patient. TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background After pulsed dye laser (PDL) treatment, facial lateral port-wine stains (PWS) clear quicker and more completely than central PWS do. Objective We sought to investigate whether the difference in the efficacy of the treatment between central and lateral facial PWS was related to different histologic manifestations. Method Thirteen patients with PWS had biopsies and underwent PDL treatments in both central and lateral areas of the face. The hypothesis was tested by correlating the PWS response to PDL with the depth and diameter of the PWS vessels. The clinical efficacy was assessed by chromameter 2 months after the final PDL treatment, whereas diameter and depth of PWS vessels were measured in biopsy specimens. Results All patients were treated on central and lateral facial sites. The chromameter evaluation showed that the average blanching rate was 34.01% and 8.68% for lateral and central facial sites, respectively (P <.05), which suggests a better response to PDL treatment in the lateral than in the central area. Histologic manifestations showed that vessels in the lateral regions were primarily located in the papillary dermis, whereas in the central regions they were extensively distributed from the dermis into the subcutaneous tissue. Limitations The small number of cases included in this study and the lack of follow-up longer than 2 months constitute limitations. Conclusion Lateral facial PWS respond better to PDL than PWS located in the central face. Differences in vessel location and diameter may be responsible for the variations in PWS response to PDL. TY  - JOUR
AB  - Objective: Laser Doppler imaging (LDI) and laser speckle imaging (LSI) are two major optical techniques aiming at non-invasively imaging the skin blood perfusion. However, the relationship between perfusion values determined by LDI and LSI has not been fully explored. Methods: 8 healthy volunteers and 13 PWS patients were recruited. The perfusions in normal skin on the forearm of 8 healthy volunteers were simultaneously measured by both LDI and LSI during post-occlusive reactive hyperemia (PORH). Furthermore, the perfusions of port wine stains (PWS) lesions and contralateral normal skin of 10 PWS patients were also determined. In addition, the perfusions for PWS lesions from 3 PWS patients were successively monitored at 0, 10 and 20 min during vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (V-PDT). The average perfusion values determined by LSI were compared with those of LDI for each subject. Results: In the normal skin during PORH, power function provided better fits of perfusion values than linear function: powers for individual subjects go from 1.312 to 1.942 (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.8967-0.9951). There was a linear relationship between perfusion values determined by LDI and LSI in PWS and contralateral normal skin (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.7308-0.9623), and in PWS during V-PDT (R<sup>2</sup> = 0.8037-0.9968). Conclusion: The perfusion values determined by LDI and LSI correlate closely in normal skin and PWS over a broad range of skin perfusion. However, it still suggests that perfusion range and characteristics of the measured skin should be carefully considered if LDI and LSI measures are compared. Copyright © 2015 Elsevier B.V.

AB  - Objective: To explore the clinical feature and imaging characteristics of Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS). Methods: Six patients were diagnosised as KTS by clinical and imaging examination, and then the medical records and imaging data was reviewed retrospectively. Results: Unilateral limb hypertrophy was found in 6 patients, including 5 cases in the calf, 1 case in the entire lower limb. Port wine stain of lower limbs and abdomen were found in 5 cases. MRI showed superficial varicose veins of lower limbs in 4 cases, soft tissue hemangioma in 3 cases, hyperplasia of skull diploe and pia mater hemangioma in 1 case. Conclusion: MRI can be used to show the vascular lesions and its relationship with the surrounding tissue in patients with KTS accurately, and evaluate the hypertrophy of bone and soft tissue. TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background: Mixed vascular nevus (or nevus vascularis mixtus) represents an admixture of cutaneous vascular malformations of the telangiectatic type and angiospastic spots of nevus anemicus. It can occur as an purely cutaneous trait or as a hallmark of a neurocutaneous phenotype (mixed vascular nevus syndrome) characterised by the combination of: (I) paired vascular (telangiectatic and anemic) twin nevi and brain abnormalities of the Dyke-Davidoff-Masson type (i.e., crossed cerebral/cerebellar hemiatrophy with hypoplasia of the ipsilateral cerebral vessels and homolateral hypertrophy of the skull and sinuses (hyperpneumatisation) with contralateral hemispheric hypertrophy); or (II) paired vascular twin nevi and brain malformations of the Dyke-Davidoff-Masson type in association with systemic abnormalities consisting in facial asymmetry, skeletal anomalies (i.e., Legg-Calve-Perthes-like disease) and disorders of autoimmunity (i.e., diabetes, thyroiditis). In 2014, Happle proposed to name the syndrome with the eponym Ruggieri-Leech syndrome. Methods: Review of the existing literature on nevus vascularis mixtus and information on our personal experience on new cases and follow-up of previously reported cases by some of us. Results: The existing literature revealed 4 previous studies including 33 cases with an inferred purely cutaneous trait and 3 cases with a combination of paired vascular twin nevi and brain malformation of the Dyke-Davidoff-Masson type. Our personal experience includes 4 unpublished patients (1 female and 3 males; currently aged 2 to 34 years) seen and followed-up at our Institutions in Italy who had: paired vascular nevi involving either the face (n=2) or the face and parts of the body (n=2); facial asymmetry (n=4); mild to moderate facial dysmorphic features (n=2); developmental delay (n=3); seizures/stroke-like episodes and associated hemiplegia (n=4); muscular hypotrophy (n=2); mild to moderate hemispheric atrophy (n=4); skull osseous hypertrophy (n=4); hyperpneumatisation of the sinuses (n=2); hypoplastic brain vessels (n=4); colpocephaly and malformation of cortical development (n=2). Follow-up data on our previous 2 cases revealed that the vascular abnormalities in the skin and nervous system were stable over years without neurological progression or deterioration. Conclusions: Pathogenically, this complex phenotype suggests that embryonic pairing and somatic recombination of recessive (didymotic) alleles controlling the balance between constriction (i.e., nevus anemicus) and dilatation (i.e., nevus telangiectaticus) of blood vessels could be the primary event causing the phenomena of cutaneous and brain vascular twin spotting and the paired phenomena of skull hyperpneumatisation vs. hypertrophy and brain megalencephaly/colpocephaly vs. cortical dysplasia. This association is likely more frequent than previously thought and should be investigated by means of: (I) brain and spinal cord imaging (combination of CT and MRI studies); (II) skeletal X-ray studies (when dictated by clinical findings); (III) systemic ultrasound studies; (IV) neurophysiologic studies (EEG); (V) psychomotor testing; (VI) and laboratory investigation (including immune-mediated dysfunction). AB  - Introduction: King Richard the Third has always been an historical controversial figure. The literary clinical-like description of his physical features (hypertrophy of one of the king's lower limbs, deformities including facial, ostheosclerosis and hemangiomes) along with the recent (2015) discovery of his skeleton under a parking area in Leicester suggest that the king could be affected by a rare genetic angiologic disease: the Klippel Trenaunay Weber Syndrome (KTS). In this study we compare a possible KTS posthoc clinical diagnosis considering the King as a forerunner patient, with the case of a 59 years old male patient presenting both clinical and instrumental evidences of the disease at eco-color- Doppler and angio-MRI (e.g. severe widespread superficial varicous veins and collateral vessels). Methods: We considered the literary description of Richard III's physical aspects as an ante-litteram presentation of a patient affected by KTS, supported by the seemingly idiopatic scoliosis plus hypertrophy of the king's lower limb evidenced by the retrieval of his skeleton. We observed very similar clinical conditions in a 59 years-old patient presenting severe hypertrophy of the left lower limb since the age of three, hemangiomes and varicosities on the hypertrophic limb whereas the other limb presented normal size and aspect. The patient underwent a venous eco-color- Doppler of the lower limbs and an angio-MRI exam which clearly confirmed the diagnosis of KTS. We did not perform an angio-TC-scan (gold standard) due to the patient's history of throat cancer already treated with radiotherapy. Results: KTS is a genetic syndrome with onset both in children and young adults. The etiology is still unknown, although testing is ongoing: it might be associated with a translocation at t(8;14)(q22.3;q13) and with VG5Q. KTS presents three main diagnostic manifestations: nevus flammeus, venous/lymphatic malformations, and soft-tissue hypertrophy of the affected limb. Whereas the diagnosis of KTS on Richard III is of course post-hoc and purely clinical, the diagnosis of KTS on our patient is confirmed both by his clinical evidences and history and by the instrumental exams performed. The eco-color-Doppler and the angio-MRI underlined the presence of several varicosities, collateral vessels and arteriovenous fistulae, deep and superficial, making the diagnosis of KTS unassainable. (see attachments) Conclusions: "Historia magistra vitae": thanks to the retrieval of the skeleton of Richard III and his minutious literary physical characterization (Shakespeare, Thomas Moore), we could speculate a post-hoc diagnosis of KTS therefore examining in depth this interesting genetic angiologic disease. Later on, whilst following backwards the King's path, we could witness and report in this study a nowadays patient presenting the very same clinical fea-tures on whom we could perform instrumental modern exams, thus acclaring a certain diagnosis of KTS, an often unrecognized syndrome, still incredibly rare, as only 1000 cases have been reported in medical literature. Until now!,.

AB  - Pulsed dye laser (PDL) is considered as treatment of choice for cutaneous capillary malformation. The regeneration or revascularization of blood vessels after PDL treatment is one of the causes of treatment failures which may be explained by angiogenesis via the induction of the hypoxia inducible factor-1a (HIF-1alpha) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) pathways. Recently, topical administration of rapamycin (RPM), which is also known as sirolimus, was introduced as a possible adjunctive therapeutic option to minimize post-laser revascularization in facial capillary malformations. We evaluated the effect of combined use of 1% topical RPM with PDL compared to PDL alone in cutaneous capillary malformation of trunk or extremities and tried to identify the effective length of RPM application. The study design was a prospective side-by-side comparison of 5 patients. Three adjacent areas of cutaneous capillary malformation which had never been treated before were selected in each patient and underwent the following regimens: (A) PDL alone; (B) PDL + topical RPM for 1 week post-PDL; and (C) PDL + topical RPM for 8 weeks post-PDL. Each patient was treated by PDL (Vbeam Perfecta, Candela/Syneron, Wayland, MA) every 8 weeks at varied settings with the following parameters: fluence 4.75-6.25 J/cm<sup>2</sup>, pulse duration 0.45 ms, focal spot size 10 mm, 1 shot. Topical RPM was applied to the area once daily. Clinical outcomes were measured using chromameter (Minolta chromameter CR-400). Only one of five patients showed clinical improvement in color of capillary malformation with combined RPM treatment. Overall, there was no statistically significant difference in redness (p = .65 at 8 weeks, p=.87 at 16 weeks by Kruskal-Wallis test) and blanching rate between PDL alone and combined topical RPM regimens. In conclusion, topical RPM does not seem to be effective as a treatment modality for port wine stains.

AB  - Objective: Sturge-Weber Syndrome (SWS) is characterised by a facial port-wine stain, leptomeningeal angiomatosis, seizures, hemiplegia and glaucoma. Patients also have cognitive, language and social communication impairments. There is no published evidence linking SWS with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD). The study aims were 1) to determine the prevalence of social communication difficulties (SCD) and ASD in the SWS population attending a specialist tertiary service, 2) to determine aetiological factors for SCD and ASD in SWS. Methods: A retrospective case note review of children with SWS, with case ascertainment from an existing database. Data collected included: descriptions of SCD and/or ASD, including standardised screening questionnaires and the Autism Diagnostic Observation Schedule (ADOS), the extent of the pial angioma, epilepsy history, language, social communication and cognitive profiles. Results: The population of 92 children with SWS (mean age=8.45y, range=1.75y to 19.08y) showed a prevalence of 44.6% with SCD and 23.9% of patients with ASD. Children with bilateral compared with unilateral pial angioma were more likely to have SCD (64.7% vs 39.2%, p=0.056) and ASD (47.1% vs 17.6%, p=0.009). Poor language abilities were significantly associated with SCD (p=0.021) and ASD (p=0.005), while poor cognitive skills were shown to not be a strong predictor. The presence of epilepsy showed no correlation with SCD or ASD. The average age of epilepsy onset did not differ between those with or without SCD (p=0.926) and those with or without ASD (p=0.155). A history of status epilepticus showed no statistically significant difference in relation to SCD (p=0.897) or ASD (p=0.420). Conclusions: The results show children with SWS, especially those with poor language have a high prevalence of SCD and ASD. The lack of evidence of a relationship with epilepsy variables suggests that the underlying disorder is the major determinant of SCD and ASD.

AB  - Background: Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome (BWS) is a congenital overgrowth disorder predisposing to tumorigenesis that results from abnormal expression or function of imprinted genes of chromosome 11p15.5. Methods: Forty-seven patients in Taiwan with clinical suspicion ofBWS were referred for diagnostic testing based on methylation profiling of H19- associated imprinting center (IC) 1 and KCNQ1OT1-associated IC2 using high-resolution melting analysis, multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification, or high-resolution quantitative methylation profiling. Results: Twenty-eight patients received a clinical diagnosis of BWS (the presence of 3 major features or 2 major features and at least 1 minor feature), 18 had suspected BWS (the presence of at least 1 major feature), and 1 had isolated Wilms' tumor. Nineteen patients were identified with IC2 hypomethylation (including 1 with isolated Wilms' tumor), 1 with IC1 hypermethylation, 2 with paternal uniparental disomy, and 1 with CDKN1C mutation. Several clinical features were found to be statistically different (P < 0.05) between the 2 groups-clinical diagnosis of BWS (n = 28) or suspected BWS (n = 18)-including macroglossia, pre- or postnatal gigantism, abdominal wall defect, ear creases, facial nevus flammeus, BWS score, and the molecular diagnosis rate. Molecular lesion was detected in 81 % of patients with the presence of three major features, compared with 33 % and 28 % of those with two or one major feature, respectively. The mean BWS score was 5.6 for 19 subjects with "IC2 hypomethylation", compared with 3.8 for 2 subjects with pUPD. The BWS score of one subject with CDKN1C mutation and one with IC1 hypermethylation was 6 and 7, respectively. Discusssion: The BWS score was positively correlated with the molecular diagnosis rate (P < 0.01). The BWS database of epigenotype, genotype, and phenotype is expected to promote better genetic counseling and medical care of these patients.

AB  - Background: The treatment of port-wine stains is codified with a preference of the pulsed dye laser represents the gold standard. Cases of laser resistance are in the order of about 30%. AB  - Background: Recently, a nonsynonymous single-nucleotide variant (c.548G-[A, p.Arg183Gln) activating mutation in GNAQ was detected in 88% of pathologic tissue samples of patients with Sturge-Weber syndrome (SWS) and in 92% from non-syndromic port-wine stains (PWS). Objectives: As this result support the hypothesis that PWS are cutaneous mosaics, our group did a study in order to redefine the topography of upper facial PWS and the risk of SWS. Methods: We conducted a multicenter study in 8 university hospital departments of dermatology in France. Children less than 1 year of age with a facial PWS involving all or part of the upper aspect of the face, with a surface area of at least 1 cm2, were prospectively recruited. All patients underwent cerebral MRI during the first year of life. Facial photographs were systematically taken for each child. A diagnosis of SWS was defined as an upper facial PWS with neurologic manifestations during clinical follow-up and cerebral MRI signs. Patients with a median frontofacial capillary malformation (nevus simplex) and those without cerebral MRI before 1 year of age, or at least 6 months of follow-up, were excluded. Results: 71 patients were examined of whom 66 were included in the study. Careful analysis of the facial PWS templates allowed us to clearly identify 6 major patterns of distribution (figure). Patterns 2 (fron-to-temporal), 5 (hemifacial) and 6 (median) were possibly associated with SWS. On the contrary, patterns 1 (linear nonmedian), 3 (isolated cheek and canthus) and 4 (combined linear and cheek) were not. Interestingly, the nonmedian linear pattern (pattern 1) concerned 20 patients (30%of the study population) and was never associated with SWS despite forehead involvement. Discussion: Facial PWS patterns conform to areas of postzygotic mosaicism and the classical terminology stipulating ophthalmic division of trigeminal nerve territory involvement in SWS should be abandoned. Early somatic mutation of the craniofacial complex (frontonasal prominence, forebrain, leptomeninx) could account for the abnormal development of the vasculature responsible for SWS, whereas a similar but later somatic mutation could result in cutaneous non-syndromic PWS. The nonmedian linear pattern fits the facial Blaschko linear pattern observed in cutaneous hamartoma, or in blaschkitis. This distribution probably corresponds to a superficial PWS due a very late mutation of a limited cell population originating from the neural crest. Conclusion: Infants with an isolated nonmedian linear facial PWS require only clinical follow- up, as this pattern probably corresponds to a blashkolinear mosaicism and is not associated with SSW.

AB  - Background: Cutis marmorata telangiectatica congenita (CMTC) is a sporadic, highly characteristic vascular malformation mainly involving the capillaries and venules. The incidence of CMTC is probably underestimated as it is quite frequently seen in a pediatric dermatology service. However, congenital smooth muscle hamartoma (SMH) is a rare condition. It typically presents as a solitary, skin-colored or hyperpigmented patch or indurated plaque, sometimes with associated hypertrichosis. Results: A two-month-old boy was referred for the evaluation of a congenital lesion on his leg. At first sight - before palpation of the lesion - he seemed to have CMTC in a band-like distribution along the lateral aspect of his right leg and foot with partial atrophy of the involved area. However, even without touching the skin we observed vermiform movement of the affected skin and sudden marked patchy whitening within the band-like lesion which spontaneously resolved within 30-40 s. On palpation there was a firm indurated linear plaque in association with the livedo-like, partially atrophic skin. A skin biopsy was performed and the histology was consistent with a smoothmuscle hamartoma with fascicles of spindle cells and positive immunohistochemical staining for smooth-muscle-actin. At the last follow-up at the age of 10 months the child continued to be asymptomatic with a similar presentation of his SMH with CMTC-like feature, however the periodic spontaneous smooth muscle contractions were less visible. Conclusion: We were intrigued by the unusual presentation of this case with CMTC- like features on top of a congenital SMH. However, we were able to find a single, strikingly similar case in the literature. Vivehanantha et al. had recently described a congenital smooth muscle hamartoma masquerading as a reticulate vascular nevus on the leg. The clinical picture as well as the histology strongly resembles our patient. It remains unclear, whether the vascular component is fully caused by the SMH or if the CMTC-like aspect occurs superimposed on the SMH. We advised for a conservative approach because of the benign nature and rather large extension of this lesion.

AB  - Objectives and study: Phacomatosis pigmentovascularis (PPV) is a rare congenital disorder characterised by cutaneous vascular and melanocytic lesions. PPV may affect many organ systems and clinical expression may have a wide variability. We report a case of a four-year-old girl who has PPV and was referred to our department due to iron deficiency anemia. This four-year-old girl was diagnosed with phacomatosis cesioflammea (a subgroup of PPV) as she had nevus of ota, nevus flammeus, mongolian spots and nevus anemicus. A blood count test performed due to pallor and heart palpitations and was consistent with anemia as her hemoglobin level was 4.6 g/dl. The patient was thoroughly investigated for anemia, and laboratory tests were consistent with iron deficiency anemia. The patient received an erythrocyte transfusion and iron therapy over three months. Control blood tests showed that the patient was still anemic, even after given iron treatment. An occult blood test with stool was positive. The patient referred to our department with iron deficiency anemia. Endoscopy was performed to investigate the cause of the anemia. An upper endoscopy revealed vascular tortuosity, telangiectasia in the stomach and fragile mucosa. A Doppler ultrasound was performed to determine whether portal venous abnormalities existed, but the ultrasound was normal. Conclusion: PPV is a rare disorder which coexistence of a pigmented nevus and cutaneous vascular malformations. The diagnosis of this syndrome is primarily clinical and classified into five main groups. To our knowledge, this is the first case of phacomatosis pigmentovascularis in which the patient displays symptoms of iron refractory anemia due to occult gastrointestinal bleeding from vascular lesions in the stomach and the second part of the duodenum.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background: The pulsed dye laser (PDL) is currently treatment of choice for port wine stains (PWS). However, some PWS are recalcitrant to treatment. One mechanism for PDL resistance is inadequate heat generation within larger PWS blood vessels. This study combines PDL with radiofrequency energy (RF) into one device to target deeper vessels and overcome PDL resistance. Adding RF, treatment of recalcitrant PWS without increases in PDL fluence is possible without compromising safety. Study: A prospective investigation of a novel device combining RF with PDL was initiated to treat recalcitrant PWS. Ten large recalictrant PWS were divided into 5 treatment areas: PDL alone, RF alone, PDL followed by RF (PDL+RF), RF followed by PDL (RF+PDL), and untreated control. Subjects underwent a maximum of 6 treatments, 4-6 weeks apart, with follow-up at 12 weeks. Pain and skin assessment were evaluated as well as subject and investigator satisfaction. Photography was performed at all visits. Biopsies were performed on selected subjects. Results: Age ranged from 29-55 years, skin types I-IV. Areas treated with RF+PDL and PDL+RF had significant and lasting improvement on blinded reviews of photographs in 70% of the treated areas compared PDL alone. Pain scores were greater in the RF+PDL and PDL+RF treated areas compared to PDL. However, the safety profile of RF+PDL and PDL+RF treated areas was identical to PDL alone. Investigator and subjects' rating improvement were greatest for RF+PDL and PDL+RF areas compared to the PDL alone. The drastic improvement persisted with additional long term follow up over 6 months, noting consistent clearance with the RF+PDL above all other areas. Histology showed deeper damage to blood vessels for RF+PDL and PDL+RF treated areas as compared to all other areas. Conclusion: This long term follow up demonstrates that the combination of PDL and RF provides superior outcomes compared to PDL alone for large recalcitrant PWS.

TY  - JOUR
AB  - Background: Pulsed dye laser (PDL) represents a standard treatment for port wine stains (PWS). However, approximately 20% of patients respond poorly and yield unsatisfactory end results. A number of smaller studies have assessed Alexandrite laser treatment for PWS, showing good effect. The optimal Alexandrite laser parameters are however not known. The aim of this study therefore was to assess clinical efficacy and safety of Alexandrite treatment for deep red to purple PWS at different pulse durations. Study: Fifteen individuals with deep red, purple macular or hypertrophic PWS were included. Four equally sized test areas were marked within each PWS. Three test areas were randomized to receive one treatment with pulse durations of 3, 5 or 10 milliseconds (ms), 8mmspot, DCD 60/40, while the fourth was left untreated. The lowest effective fluence to create purpura within the entire laser test spot was titrated and applied to interventional areas. Standardized clinical photographs were taken prior to, immediately after laser treatment and at 6-8 weeks follow-up. Clinical efficacy and treatment-related side effects were assessed using clinical photos. Results: Effect, ranging from slight to near-complete clearance, was observed for 14/15 patients treated with 3ms pulse duration. Though less prominent, effect was also present with pulse durations of 5 and 10 ms. More than 50% clearance was achieved in 5 of 7 patients with purple, hypertrophic PWS, in 1 of 4 patients with purple, macular PWS and in 1 of 4 patients with deep red PWS(3ms pulse duration). Four individuals developed side effects in the form of hypopigmentation and/or atrophic scaring, mainly associated with 5 and 10ms pulse durations. Conclusion: A 3ms pulse duration appears safer than longer pulse durations. Alexandrite laser treatment should be restricted to experienced personnel due to a particularly narrow therapeutic window.
